title: Speed and distance-time graphs
cover_sub: Speed, distance and time are one formula three ways round. Secure the calculations, extend to graphs, units and average speed, then master velocity-time graphs and meeting problems.

levels_long.s: Speed, distance and time, and reading a distance-time graph.
levels_long.e: Unit conversions, density, average speed over two stages, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Velocity-time graphs, pressure, and two objects moving at once.

briefing: Speed = distancetime. Rearranged: distance = speed × time, and time = distancespeed. The units must match: km and hours give km/h; metres and seconds give m/s.
On a distance-time graph, the gradient is the speed and a flat section means stopped. On a speed-time graph, the gradient is the acceleration and the area underneath is the distance travelled.
method: Write the formula you need, rearranged for the unknown.
Check the units: convert minutes to hours, or km to m, before you calculate.
For a graph: read values carefully at grid lines, then use gradient or area.
Give units with every answer, and turn decimal hours into minutes if asked.

example.question: A patrol car drives 45 km in 36 minutes. Find its average speed in km/h.
steps: The answer is in km/h, so change the time to hours: 36 minutes = 3660 = 0.6 hours.
Speed = distancetime = 450.6.

questions.tip: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time. It is not the average of 30 and 45.

text: Leo worked out the speed of a car that travels 45 km in 30 minutes. Find his mistake and give the correct speed.
questions.working: He divided by minutes, not hours: 45 ÷ 0.5.

text: Use the speed-time graph. Work out the car's acceleration in the first 4 seconds.
A crate rests on a face of area 0.4 m², exerting a pressure of 300 N/m².
It is turned onto a face of area 0.15 m². Find the new pressure.
Two suspects are 270 km apart. They drive towards each other, starting at the same time, at 80 km/h and 100 km/h.
How far has the slower car travelled when they meet?
questions.working: They close the gap at 180 km/h: 270 ÷ 180 = 1.5 h. 80 × 1.5.

text: A train 200 m long travels at 90 km/h through a tunnel 1.3 km long. How long does it take from the front entering to the back leaving the tunnel?

closed_points: Use speed = distance ÷ time in all three arrangements.
Convert between hours and minutes, and between km/h and m/s.
Read speed from the gradient of a distance-time graph.
Find distance from the area under a speed-time graph, and acceleration from its gradient.
Use density and pressure with the same formula triangle idea.
